turns.prompt: when I end a meeting, the recap leaves out any task that has a person on it but no deadline. like if they say 'Priya will send the contract' with no date it just isnt in the action items. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
I changed the prompts so owner-only tasks like "Priya will send the contract" should now show up in the recap. I haven't run it against a real meeting, so that part is untested.

There was no code filtering anything out. The instructions to the model were the cause. The default and Groq summary prompts never said a deadline was optional. The Groq prompt's only example was "Bob: Draft invite copy by Wednesday", and the Team Meet capture format was `📋 [Who] to [What] by [When]`. The model took that to mean an item needs a date, so it dropped the ones without one.

What I changed:
- **`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`**: The shared rules block now tells the model to include every task someone commits to or is assigned, even with no date. It should only add a date if one was actually said. This block feeds both the default prompt and the mode-based prompts. I also rewrote the default prompt's `actionItems` line to say "Owner: task" with a deadline not required.
- **`electron/llm/prompts.ts`**: The Groq summary prompt now has a no-date example ("Priya: Send the contract") and says a deadline isn't required.
- **`electron/llm/tinyPrompts.ts`**: The Team Meet capture format now says to drop "by [When]" when no date was given, and to keep the item anyway. The tiny JSON summary prompt now has the same owner-without-date rule.

The other long prompts in `prompts.ts` already told the model to keep owner-only items, so I left those alone.

This is a wording fix to a model's behavior, so it could still miss an item now and then. To check it, end a short test meeting where someone says "Priya will send the contract". Also, `data.context` is cut to 10,000 characters before summarizing (`MeetingPersistence.ts:207`). In a long meeting, tasks said late in the call can drop out for that reason alone. I didn't change that.

I found the real cause this time, and I've fixed it. I couldn't type-check or run any of it: there's no `node_modules` here, and the sandbox blocked the npm download.

My first fix only touched the summary that's saved when a meeting ends. The recap you see is a separate pipeline, `RecapLLM`, and I hadn't looked at it. Two things in it dropped your tasks:
- **Shared 3-5 bullet budget:** The recap prompt asked for "3-5 concise bullets" covering decisions, action items and open questions together. A date-less task like "Priya will send the contract" was the easiest thing to cut.
- **Hard cap of 5 bullets:** `clampRecapResponse` in `RecapLLM.ts` threw away everything after the 5th bullet, even if the model had listed more tasks.

What I changed:
- **Separate action items:** In `electron/llm/prompts.ts`, all six recap prompts now share one `RECAP_INSTRUCTION`. It asks for 3-5 summary bullets on decisions and open questions. Every action item then gets its own extra bullet, like `📋 Priya: Send the contract`. A deadline is optional, and the model should add "by <date>" only if one was actually said.
- **Tiny-model prompt:** In `tinyPrompts.ts`, `TINY_RECAP_PROMPT` has the same rule. Its past-tense rule would have turned tasks into "Priya took on…", so I exempted the `📋` lines from it.
- **Clamp fix:** In `RecapLLM.ts`, `clampRecapResponse` now keeps every `📋` bullet and caps only the summary bullets at 5. A `📋` line the model writes without a leading dash still counts as a bullet.

The earlier changes to the saved end-of-meeting summary are still in place, so both paths now follow the same rule.

Please end a test meeting where someone says "Priya will send the contract" with no date. Check that it appears as a `📋` bullet in the recap.

If it's still missing, tell me which place you're looking: the live recap, the saved meeting page, or the follow-up email. That will show which path is still dropping it. I haven't touched the follow-up email prompt.

I've fixed one more real bug, but I haven't reproduced your problem, and I'm not sure this is the cause. Nothing has been run. There's no `node_modules` here and the sandbox blocks npm, so I can't type-check or test.

The new fix is in the end-of-meeting summary in `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`. It sent the model only the first 10,000 characters of the transcript, which is roughly 2,500 tokens. Anything said after that point never reached the model. Tasks like "Priya will send the contract" usually come up in the wrap-up, so they were being cut off before the model saw them, whatever the prompt said. Now:
- **Cap:** The cap is 40,000 characters.
- **Long meetings:** It keeps the first 20% and the last 80%, with a marker where the middle was dropped.
- **Small models:** It then runs through the existing `fitContextForCurrentModel`, which drops the oldest lines if the active model's window is smaller.

That makes three layers I've now touched. The first two rounds fixed the prompts that decide what counts as an action item, and the second also fixed the live recap's 5-bullet cap.

I've now checked the display, PDF, email and storage code, and none of it filters action items.

I'm not going to guess a fourth time. These would let me find the real cause:
1. **Where you see the item missing:** the live recap during the meeting, the meeting page after you end it, or the follow-up email.
2. **Which mode and AI provider you use:** for example Team Meet, and whether it's Groq, Claude, Ollama or a custom provider.
3. **A case that fails:** the exact transcript lines, and roughly how far into the meeting they were said.

If you can run the app, the console logs would settle it. `[MeetingPersistence] Raw LLM summary response` prints what the model returned. If Priya's task is already missing there, the model dropped it. If it's in that log but not on screen, something downstream is dropping it, and I'll look there.
